response.text: {"question":"How does tuberculosis transmit in Ethiopia and which parameters and interventions drive its spread and control under real-world data from 2011–2021?","mechanism":"An SVEITRS compartmental model with susceptible, vaccinated, exposed, infectious, treated and recovered classes, with recruitment, vaccination, loss of vaccine and recovered immunity, progression from exposed to infectious, treatment and disease-induced deaths, and homogeneous mixing.","modelEquations":["eq1"],"result":{"text":"The model shows TB persists in Ethiopia with R0>1 and can be eliminated when R0<1 through vaccination, treatment and reduced transmission.","quote":"The model's stability analysis indicated that there is a disease-free equilibrium in areas where the basic reproduction number ($\\mathscr{R}_0$) is less than one."},"findings":[{"kind":"result","text":"Maximum likelihood estimation gives more accurate and reliable parameter estimates than nonlinear least squares on synthetic and real data.","quote":"Model parameters were estimated via two methods: nonlinear least squares and maximum likelihood, with maximum likelihood providing more accurate and reliable results, as confirmed by a test case."},{"kind":"threshold","text":"The disease-free equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable when the effective reproduction number is below one, preventing an epidemic.","quote":"If $\\mathscr{R}_v< 1$, then the disease-free equilibrium point is locally asymptotically stable, i.e., no tuberculosis epidemic can develop in the population."},{"kind":"result","text":"With estimated Ethiopian parameters the basic reproduction number is 2.67, indicating ongoing transmission.","quote":"We obtained $\\mathscr{R}_0 = 2.67$ for the estimated model parameters, which are greater than one, indicating that the tuberculosis is continuously multiplying."},{"kind":"conclusion","text":"Higher natural death, vaccination, treatment and disease death rates lower TB, while higher recruitment, contact, infection rates and loss of vaccine protection increase spread.","quote":"Sensitivity analysis revealed important factors affecting TB levels: higher natural death rates, vaccination rates, treatment rates, and disease-related death rates lower TB cases, whereas higher recruitment rates, contact rates, infection rates, and loss of vaccine protection increase its spread."},{"kind":"result","text":"Increasing the treatment rate of infectious individuals reduces the infected population and may lead to eradication locally.","quote":"The result revealed that the infectious population decreases as the treatment rate of infected individuals increases; in the long run, this may lead to the eradication of the disease from the community."}]}
